ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, an Earth schematic circle can be seen, and the dashed great circle is elliptical; point A is at the left end, point B is at the right end, point O is in the middle, and A, O, and B lie on the same straight line. Point P is located on the upper-left outer circle; the segment OP is drawn in the figure, and 15° is marked between the directions of OP and OA. Therefore, OB and OA are in opposite directions, and ∠POB can be read as 180°−15°=165°. Then reason: The question states that point P has an Earth rotation linear velocity of 0, indicating that P is an Earth pole; it also says P is located on land. The North Pole is mainly ocean, while the South Pole is land, so P is the South Pole. Point B “east of it is the Western Hemisphere, west of it is the Eastern Hemisphere,” which exactly corresponds to the Eastern and Western Hemisphere dividing line at 160°E, so the longitude of point B is 160°E. The central angle from the South Pole to a point at northern latitude equals 90° plus that point’s northern latitude. From the figure, ∠POB=165°, so 165°=90°+latitude, latitude=75°, and it is north latitude. Therefore, the coordinates of point B are 75°N, 160°E.
